findings.reason: the section should extend the existing `review_required`/waiver path and key its class rule to it, rather than introduce a parallel flag that can drift from the guard that already fires.
findings.text: §2 proposes "a review-required flag that crew complete honours by refusing promotion without a scored review from another lane", but promotion.py already computes `review_required` (line 4932) and refuses an unreviewed promotion naming both revisions (promotion.py:5106), with `--waive-unreviewed-promotion REASON` (line 5149) as the override — the plan's new flag is a second owner of one decision

findings.reason: §2f's first done-when item is already satisfied by its owner; the section should record it as landed and narrow the node to the two items that remain (a member-in-flight refusal naming a free member, and `crew observe` not recommended without a run id).
findings.text: §2f's done-when asks for "a lane document reported field by field, each present value carried and each absent one marked absent … requiring headroom to read 4 rather than unknown", but lane_document.py already resolves every field independently ("a missing precondition costs its own field and never the whole document", lane_document.py:6-10), and dispatch.py `_lane_reading_carry` (dispatch.py:3919) now collapses the carry only on a document-level defect (absent/unparseable `observed_at`, or a stale reading) while a null `binding_observed` costs only its own field — the defect §2f quotes (`binding_observed: null` discarding headroom at dispatch.py:1890) no longer reproduces

findings.reason: the section's premise (any named path is charged at full size) is false in the current tree, so the node must be re-derived from a reproduced failure or dropped; only the "refusal reports which inputs it counted and their sizes" half may remain open.
findings.text: §2g's done-when ("a file named only in prose is not charged … a declared write path is still charged … dedup and directory behaviours pinned") is already the contract of `_declared_input_files` (routing.py:3122), whose docstring states "A path a brief merely names is not a read … A path counts only when the clause naming it also declares it an input", with exclusion-verb handling `_GOVERNING_VERB` (routing.py:62) and dedup/`counted` bookkeeping in `_context_file_inputs` (routing.py:3165) — the plan even says these are "already right, and should not be broken fixing this"

findings.reason: the section must justify a new axis or extend `resolve_role`/bar.py's overlay; a parallel routing layer over the same role+spec+class resolution drifts from the one `resolve_role` performs today.
findings.text: §2 puts a per-class, per-lane rule in flight config; the config already carries two node-shape routing axes — role overlays by `by_spec_level` and `by_capability_class` (reckon/crew/routing.py:90,108; resolve_role routing.py:149) — and a lane recommendation already exists in bar.py ("advise, never route", bar.py:27) that turns node open-endedness into `send-local`/`send-metered`. The plan adds a third axis and does not say why the existing overlay mechanism or the bar cannot carry the class rule

findings.reason: the section must account for the added refusal family and override surface in its own text — either fold the class refusal into an existing family (the D17/D03 lane-selection family) or state why the ruling needs its own, and name the config key that carries the class→lane rule so the interface budget is explicit.
findings.text: §2's refusal "names the class, the lane and the audit row that set the rule" and a coordinator override "lands on the ledger row", so the section adds a refusal family to the registry (reckon/crew/refusals.py, 23 families D01–D23) and a dispatch override option, and names nothing it retires or merges

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the landed prescription judgement (reckon/crew/prescription.py:130) is a genuine deep module: one public function hiding the five-property ruling, with the path helpers private.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2, §2f and §2g each re-implement machinery with an existing owner: promotion.py's unreviewed-promotion guard, lane_document.py's per-field reader, and routing.py's declared-input extractor.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §2 adds a refusal family (a class-of-work routing refusal, and an override that lands on the ledger row) without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites plans (crew-effort-routing, effort-calibration, scoring-should-stop-a-promotion) but names no mechanism or file it extends, and two sections (§2f, §2g) propose behaviour the codebase already implements.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §2 adds a class-of-work routing axis in flight config beside the existing role overlays and the bar's lane recommendation without stating why they cannot be extended.
